newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE might peg dirham to basket of currencies.
newsitem.headline: UAE might peg dirham to basket of currencies.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates said on Sunday "serious thought" should be given to linking its dollar-pegged dirham to a basket of currencies.
"There has to be serious thought about linking the dirham to a basket of currencies," state-run news agency WAM quoted Minister of Finance and Industrial Affairs Ahmed bin Humaid al-Tayer as saying.

"The single European Currency might give more weight to European currencies, but the issue (of pegging to a basket of currencies) needs coordination on the level of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states."

Regional currency traders say the GCC, a political and economic alliance grouping Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, the UAE and Kuwait, have debated such a move for over a decade. But they have failed to reach a consensus on delinking.
All, except Kuwait which links its dinar to a basket of currencies, peg their units to the dollar. Their oil sale prices are denominated in dollars.
The dirham has been pegged at 3.67 to the dollar since 1980.
Tayer said the ministry had concluded a study on "this matter" but he gave no further details.
A study prepared by the ministry's investment department last year recommended the dirham be linked to a basket of currencies rather than the dollar, citing foregone earnings.
It said trade losses incurred by the UAE government from 1986 to 1994 because of the dollar link topped $13 billion.
The study also called for a review of oil pricing formula, recommending that it be based on a currency basket.
Other OPEC producers, notably Iran, have previously called for a reduction in producers' vulnerability to swings in the international value of the dollar on which oil-trade is based world-wide.
